reason: The cited evidence shows that principal element segregation and embrittlement occur in HEAs at intermediate temperatures (E2), but it attributes this to thermal annealing and grain refinement, not to deformation-driven diffusion. No evidence supports the claim that plastic deformation accelerates diffusion to cause nanosegregation, nor that embrittlement occurs without intermetallic precipitates; E2 explicitly links embrittlement to brittle intermetallic phase formation.
premises: Plastic deformation at intermediate temperatures drives dislocation-assisted diffusion of principal elements to grain boundaries in HEAs.
This enhanced diffusion overcomes the alloy's sluggish kinetics, enabling rapid nanosegregation.
Nanosegregation of principal elements at grain boundaries reduces cohesion and triggers brittle intergranular cracking.
This embrittlement occurs without the formation of large intermetallic precipitates.
The degree of embrittlement correlates with the severity of imposed deformation conditions.
